_about: Typed texts for 04_build/data (main merges): models3d_curated.json models[slug]; models3d_caveats.json rows (append); models3d_combined.json models[slug]. Written 2026-10-10 by the Narrowneck 3D agent. ev lists are empty on purpose (nothing to verify). Token paths use version ids with hyphens (versions/photo_2020-08-08/...): if the token filler rejects them, replace by literals.

narrowneck-gold-coast.state_short: Renewed reef as left in June 2018 (84 containers added around the 2004-revised structure; about 534 containers placed since 1999), drawn as the visible container field of the 8 Aug 2020 aerial (default; a lower bound). Four more outlines are selectable: Option 2 renewal design 2017, 2004 revised design, 2011 survey relief zone, Navionics 4.0 m shoals (outline only). History (1999 build, 2004 weir and wings, 2017-18 renewal, Option 2 only partly built) is notes, not modelled.
narrowneck-gold-coast.ve_note: At VE = 5 a 1.5:1 container flank looks like 0.3:1 and the 2 m mound height looks 10 m high.

caveat_rows.stated: 534 containers x about 147 m3 sand = about 78,500 m3 placed (Jackson 2007 p.4; Jackson 2012 p.3; City 2020)
caveat_rows.reason: The model shows only the exposed mound seen in the photo and the 2017 multibeam (relief 1-2.5 m); containers are partly buried, stacked, displaced or lost, and the envelope includes gaps.
caveat_rows.resolve: Container-by-container multibeam or the City as-built; a post-renewal survey.

caveat_rows.model: crest -2.2 m AHD = 1.44 m below LAT (MSQ AHD = LAT + 0.760)
caveat_rows.stated: papers: -2.5 m AHD = -1.5 m LAT, i.e. AHD = LAT + 1.00
caveat_rows.reason: Two datum relations for the same design crest; the model uses MSQ because it is the official benchmark and all heights are AHD-based (only the tide levels move).
caveat_rows.resolve: The offset used in the 2018 survey (City of Gold Coast / MSQ).

caveat_rows.model: {{versions/photo_2020-08-08/area_m2|n0}} m2 visible field vs {{versions/design_option2_2017/area_m2|n0}} m2 Option 2 envelope
caveat_rows.stated: design to the -6 m contour; deeper toe to about -10 m (Jackson & Corbett 2019)
caveat_rows.diff: photo field is 45 % of the design envelope
caveat_rows.reason: The toe below about -6 m is not visible on the 2020 photo; 96.6 % of the traced arms lie inside the Option 2 envelope.
caveat_rows.resolve: Post-renewal multibeam or the 2025 State bathymetric lidar.

caveat_rows.stated: stage-1 estimate 4-6 m at the -6 to -8 m toe
caveat_rows.reason: The 2017 multibeam bed at the toe is -6.5 to -7.5 m and container tops are -5 to -6 m.

caveat_rows.model: assumed smooth profile 0 / -1.8 / -2.1 m AHD at y = 0 / 100 / 190 m
caveat_rows.stated: no source resolves the surf zone here (Navionics land edge is 80 m seaward of the 2020 waterline)
caveat_rows.reason: Not part of the reef volume; affects only the look of the shore side.
caveat_rows.resolve: Navionics app and Google Earth readings (3d/REQUESTS_FOR_LIOR.md).

caveat_rows.q: Multibeam read from a colour picture
caveat_rows.model: bed and relief from Corbett Fig 3 (460 x 312 px)
caveat_rows.stated: datum and north not stated in the figure
caveat_rows.reason: Hue read through a four-tick colour bar; assumed AHD and north-up.
caveat_rows.resolve: The original multibeam grid from ICM or the City.
